source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Stress usb port with BurnIN
1. Boot into OS.
2. Install PassMark USB3 test plug on an USB port.
3. Install the latest PassMark USB3 test plug driver.
4. Make sure the FW of the PassMark USB3 test plug is latest.
5. Install the latest PassMark BurnInTest.
6. Run PassMark BurnInTest USB Test under 100% load for 3 hours.
7. Repeat 1~6 for each USB port.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: No error shown on PassMark BurnInTest, neither on PassMark USB3 test plug.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: usbutils stress-ng (loopback needs a USB-serial loopback adapter + pyserial)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "echo ---dev---; ls /dev/ttyUSB* /dev/ttyACM* 2>&1; echo ---loop---; (stty -F /dev/ttyUSB0 115200 && cat /dev/ttyUSB0 > /tmp/loop.txt & pid=$!; sleep 5; printf "USB loop" > /dev/ttyUSB0; sleep 2; kill $pid; cat /tmp/loop.txt) 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return FULL lsusb + dmesg USB lines + stress/loopback result so the user confirms the USB ports survived the stress/loopback; the full matrix over every physical port needs the operator to attach devices.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: USB stress/loopback needs physical USB devices on the specific ports; agent runs the host-side stress/loopback probe and the physical port matrix is operator.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; recognizes per-port physical setup but replaces the PassMark USB3 plug/BurnInTest workload with an unsafe assumed ttyUSB0 serial loop.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; restores the named vendor plug, driver/firmware, BurnInTest 100%/three-hour/per-port method and safety controls.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; preserves a host-side loopback concept but does not prove the required vendor stimulus or complete matrix.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms source row 207 and rejects fixed ttyUSB0 as non-equivalent and potentially wrong-device access.

original_test_intent: Verify every project-designated USB port by running the approved PassMark USB3 test plug with validated driver/firmware and the PassMark BurnInTest USB workload at 100% for three hours per port, with no tool or plug errors.
original_method: A qualified operator moves the approved PassMark USB3 test plug through the physical port matrix. For each port, the compatible driver/firmware and licensed BurnInTest profile are verified, then the 100% USB test runs for 180 minutes and its complete report is preserved.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must identify each connector and move the approved PassMark plug between ports. After each setup is confirmed, the named three-hour BurnInTest core, monitoring and evidence capture can be automated; firmware changes remain separately approval-gated.
required_inputs: Complete physical USB port/controller matrix and intended sequence
Approved PassMark USB3 plug identity, compatibility and expected plug indicators
Owner-approved driver, plug firmware target/image/hash/tool and recovery method—not an unbounded 'latest'
Licensed compatible PassMark BurnInTest build and exact 100% USB profile
Per-port maintenance duration, thermal/power limits, operator and OOB recovery
safety_requirements: Do not execute the generic ttyUSB0/stty/cat substitute; it may write to the wrong serial device and does not exercise the source method.
Do not install or flash 'latest' artifacts until exact signed targets, compatibility and recovery are approved.
Isolate boot, input, security and OOB-sensitive ports; preserve prior logs and every per-port report.
Stop on disconnect, overcurrent, controller/plug error, thermal/power excursion or service impact; never auto-retry or silently move to the next port.
agent_execution_scope: Validate port/plug/tool/driver/firmware manifests and collect USB, platform, thermal, power and BMC baselines.
After operator placement and approval, run the exact 100%/180-minute BurnInTest profile once per port and capture complete tool and plug results.
Verify post-port health, enforce stop conditions and assemble a per-port coverage report without assigning the formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve exact driver, firmware, BurnInTest and recovery manifests and any firmware change.
Physically move and identify the plug for each port and supervise hardware safety.
Review all per-port reports and issue PASS/FAIL.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The /dev/ttyUSB0 serial loop assumes device class and path, can touch the wrong device, and does not run the PassMark USB3 driver/firmware or BurnInTest workload; it is rejected.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the licensed, approved PassMark BurnInTest USB profile with the validated PassMark USB3 plug, driver and firmware; automate report export and telemetry around that exact method.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Every USB port, current approved driver/firmware, PassMark BurnInTest, 100% load, three hours per port and 15/180-minute fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.status: ORIGINAL METHOD RETAINED WITH VERSION PINNING
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Replace ambiguous 'latest' with an approved versioned manifest and run the vendor profile per mapped port with synchronized USB, plug, thermal, power and BMC evidence.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the OS/controller/plug combination covered by the approved compatibility documentation.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record exact plug identity/firmware, driver, BurnInTest build/license, OS and controller driver.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use supplied PassMark test-plug, driver/firmware and BurnInTest documentation for the approved versions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Pins exact targets and recovery and adds per-port evidence reproducibility without replacing the vendor workload.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; the full approved physical port matrix requires a separate 180-minute report per port.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Versioned vendor artifacts, port map, profile and recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Total execution time scales with port count; shared-controller coverage must not be mistaken for testing an unhandled connector.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve a reduced port set, duration or different validated firmware/tool profile. Results apply only to that plan and cannot be represented as the original every-port, three-hour coverage.
expected_evidence: SUT and physical port/controller matrix, plug identity and exact driver/firmware/tool manifest
Per-port placement timestamp and configuration proving 100% USB load for 180 minutes
Complete per-port BurnInTest report and plug error/status output
Pre/during/post USB, kernel/system/BMC, thermal and power health, restored state, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criterion consistently require the PassMark USB3 plug and BurnInTest with no errors on every port. The word 'latest' is unsafe readiness ambiguity but not contradictory test intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The named stimulus, duration, repetition and acceptance are clear. Missing vendor packages, versions and physical setup are readiness gates; the automated core after each operator setup makes the case PARTIAL.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its serial-loopback command and package list as non-equivalent while retaining its recognition of physical port setup.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees with PARTIAL and preserves its exact vendor-method, version, firmware, per-port, thermal/power and recovery requirements.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Clarifies that moving the plug is repeated setup, while each three-hour core run is automatable and verdict ownership remains separate.

review_improvement: Eliminates wrong-device serial writes, pins firmware/tool versions instead of 'latest' and makes each physical connector's full-duration evidence auditable.
independent_technical_reasoning: Unlike a hot-plug acceptance case, the physical move here establishes the environment for a later three-hour vendor-tool stress core. That core and evidence are automatable, so V3.1 classifies it PARTIAL rather than MANUAL ONLY or BLOCKED.

no_automatic_retry: A failed port run remains failed evidence. Stop, preserve the complete report and diagnose before any engineer-approved repeat, firmware change or move to another port.
